reason: Conversation 1 immediately and correctly explained that 'FD 9409' is a production date (not a model or error code), asked for the E-Nr, and gave the homeowner several realistic routes to identify the pump without a legible E-Nr (second labels, receipt/registration, reading the part number off the old pump), plus a safe replacement sequence (unplug, drain via emergency hose, check the tub-to-pump hose). Conversation 2 was slower and vaguer, calling FD 9409 a 'model series or internal code', wrongly directing him to remove the top cover to find the E-Nr, and offering no alternative identification routes before defaulting to an engineer. Both were somewhat overconfident in declaring the pump dead when a sump/hose blockage remains possible, but Conversation 1 at least flagged the tub-to-pump hose as a check; Conversation 2's redeeming point is its sensible final escalation to an engineer given he won't open the machine.
